citation: Wirbel J, Pyl PT, Kartal E, et al. 2019. Meta-analysis of fecal metagenomes reveals global microbial signatures that are specific for colorectal cancer. Nature Medicine 25:679-689
what_they_do: 8-cohort CRC metagenome meta-analysis; LASSO/LOSO classifiers. Methods: cutoff 'adjusted to yield a FPR of 0.1 on the controls' of the training data; reports FPR of that fixed cutoff on other-disease cohorts (0.09-0.13) and study-to-study FPR in Fig.3 (mean +/- SD, figure only).
what_remains_open: Fixed-FPR cutoff set on training controls is the same design as ours, but realised specificity on each held-out CRC cohort's own controls is not tabulated, not tested for overdispersion, and no re-thresholding at the new site is proposed.

citation: Thomas AM, Manghi P, Asnicar F, et al. 2019. Metagenomic analysis of colorectal cancer datasets identifies cross-cohort microbial diagnostic signatures and a link with choline degradation. Nature Medicine 25:667-678
what_they_do: Cross-dataset and LODO random-forest CRC classifiers (MetaPhlAn2, curatedMetagenomicData); cross-dataset AUC 0.50-0.86. Sens/spec only traced over many thresholds vs FOBT on a ZellerG subset.
what_remains_open: AUC-only for cross-cohort transfer; no fixed operating point per cohort.

citation: Piccinno G, Thompson KN, Manghi P, et al. 2025. Pooled analysis of 3,741 stool metagenomes from 18 cohorts for cross-stage and strain-level reproducible microbial biomarkers of colorectal cancer. Nature Medicine 31:2416-2429
what_they_do: Largest CRC LODO analysis (18 cohorts, MetaPhlAn4); LODO AUC mean 0.85 (0.71-0.97); states 'new cohorts should expect AUC ~0.85'.
what_remains_open: Still AUC-only; no statement of what specificity a new site gets at a pre-fixed cutoff. Our paper directly answers the question this paper leaves open.

citation: Pasolli E, Truong DT, Malik F, et al. 2016. Machine learning meta-analysis of large metagenomic datasets: tools and biological insights. PLoS Computational Biology 12:e1004977
what_they_do: MetAML framework; cross-study and LODO prediction across 8 diseases/2424 samples; AUC-based.
what_remains_open: Cross-cohort generalisation framed in AUC only.

citation: Duvallet C, Gibbons SM, Gurry T, Irizarry RA, Alm EJ. 2017. Meta-analysis of gut microbiome studies identifies disease-specific and shared responses. Nature Communications 8:1784
what_they_do: MicrobiomeHD: 28 case-control studies, 10 diseases; shared vs disease-specific genera; within-study classifiers (AUC).
what_remains_open: Non-specific 'shared response' implies specificity against other conditions is fragile; no operating-point analysis.

citation: Wirbel J, Zych K, Essex M, et al. 2021. Microbiome meta-analysis and cross-disease comparison enabled by the SIAMCAT machine learning toolbox. Genome Biology 22:93
what_they_do: SIAMCAT; 10,803 fecal metagenomes; naive cross-study transfer 'lost accuracy and disease specificity', fixed by control-augmentation of training sets.
what_remains_open: Loss of specificity under transfer is documented (cross-disease), but remedy is retraining with extra controls, not site-level threshold resetting with a guarantee.

citation: Zeller G, Tap J, Voigt AY, et al. 2014. Potential of fecal microbiota for early-stage detection of colorectal cancer. Molecular Systems Biology 10:766
what_they_do: First metagenomic CRC classifier; combination with FOBT raises sensitivity while maintaining specificity; validated in independent populations from other countries.
what_remains_open: Operating point validated in a few external sets; no analysis of cross-site threshold drift.

citation: Wu Y, Jiao N, Zhu R, et al. 2021. Identification of microbial markers across populations in early detection of colorectal cancer. Nature Communications 12:3063
what_they_do: Adenoma-vs-control and adenoma-vs-CRC RF classifiers on 1056 public samples; independent-cohort AUC 0.78/0.84.
what_remains_open: Adenoma endpoint, AUC only.

citation: Mei Z, Wang F, Bhosle A, et al. 2024. Strain-specific gut microbial signatures in type 2 diabetes identified in a cross-cohort analysis of 8,117 metagenomes. Nature Medicine 30:2265-2276
what_they_do: 10-cohort T2D metagenome meta-analysis; species/strain associations.
what_remains_open: Association-focused; no classifier operating point.

citation: Kartal E, Schmidt TSB, Molina-Montes E, et al. 2022. A faecal microbiota signature with high specificity for pancreatic cancer. Gut 71:1359-1372
what_they_do: PDAC metagenomic classifier (Spain discovery, Germany validation); disease specificity checked against 25 public metagenomic populations (n=5792).
what_remains_open: Specificity framed as cross-disease FPR; no per-site threshold transfer or local re-setting.

citation: Zhang Y, Cidan Y, Xu J, Li B. 2026. CRC-TrustBench: benchmarking cross-study and cross-country generalization in gut metagenomic colorectal cancer prediction. Frontiers in Microbiology 17:1971707
what_they_do: 15 studies/10 countries; LOSO/LOCO; Platt calibration fit on internal partition, conformal-style sets (coverage fell below 90/95% targets), selective abstention; fixed 0.5 threshold, no outer-test labels used.
what_remains_open: Closest microbiome paper on 'probability reliability' under cross-study shift, but per-cohort specificity at a target FPR is not reported and no target-site (label-free or few-control) threshold method is given. Shows conformal guarantees break under LOSO, which supports our motivation.

citation: Wang X, Li J, Cheng Y, et al. 2026. Microbiota-assisted screening for colorectal neoplasia: advanced adenoma as the key translational endpoint - a narrative review. American Journal of Translational Research 18(9):8227-8253
what_they_do: Narrative review: 'The chosen cut-off must be fixed in the development protocol and applied without retuning in external validation'; specificity central because small drops increase colonoscopy demand.
what_remains_open: Argues the opposite protocol (never retune). Our paper must reconcile: a fixed cut-off for validation vs a pre-specified local re-thresholding rule for deployment. Good foil.

citation: Shi H, Shafizadeh M, Rukh L, et al. 2026. Cross-cohort oral microbiome meta-analysis identifies shared OPMD-OSCC dysbiosis while machine learning exposes limits of OSCC classifier transportability. bioRxiv (preprint)
what_they_do: Nested leave-one-cohort-out OSCC classifiers on 16S data; held-out AUROC 0.78-0.81; cohort identity recoverable at 99.5% balanced accuracy.
what_remains_open: Transportability measured by AUROC; operating point not addressed. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

citation: Degregori S, Huang I, Fetcinko LH, et al. 2026. A decade-scale audit of microbiome AI-readiness. iMeta
what_they_do: PRISMA audit of 2896 microbiome studies: only 5.9% deposit per-sample disease/age/sex; 85.5% of samples not reusable for cross-cohort AI.
what_remains_open: Shows iMeta's interest in cross-cohort AI reporting standards; nothing on thresholds. Useful framing for a reporting-gap angle.

citation: Gibbons SM, Duvallet C, Alm EJ. 2018. Correcting for batch effects in case-control microbiome studies. PLoS Computational Biology 14:e1006102
what_they_do: Percentile normalisation: case features converted to percentiles of within-study controls before pooling.
what_remains_open: Uses local controls as a reference distribution, like our few-local-controls idea, but at the feature level for association testing. No classifier threshold or FPR guarantee.

citation: Wang Y, Le Cao KA. 2020 (online 2019). Managing batch effects in microbiome data. Briefings in Bioinformatics 21:1954-1970
what_they_do: Review and tutorial on sources of microbiome batch effects and how to assess or correct them.
what_remains_open: Corrects features, not decision thresholds; no deployment operating point.

citation: Ma S, Shungin D, Mallick H, et al. 2022. Population structure discovery in meta-analyzed microbial communities and inflammatory bowel disease using MMUPHin. Genome Biology 23:208
what_they_do: MMUPHin: batch normalisation and meta-analysis across 10 IBD cohorts.
what_remains_open: Needs the target batch at correction time and does not guarantee FPR at a fixed cutoff. Could serve as a baseline ('batch-correct then apply cutoff').

citation: Ling W, Lu J, Zhao N, et al. 2022. Batch effects removal for microbiome data via conditional quantile regression. Nature Communications 13:5418
what_they_do: ConQuR: two-part quantile regression that produces batch-removed counts.
what_remains_open: Feature-level; operating point not studied.

citation: Austin GI, Brown Kav A, ElNaggar S, et al. 2025. Processing-bias correction with DEBIAS-M improves cross-study generalization of microbiome-based prediction models. Nature Microbiology 10:897-911
what_they_do: Learns per-microbe, per-batch bias factors (domain adaptation) to improve cross-study prediction accuracy (AUC).
what_remains_open: Strongest 'fix the features' competitor. An editor may ask whether DEBIAS-M removes threshold drift. Untested, so we should run it as a baseline.

citation: Foxx AJ, Rivers AR. 2025. A cautionary tale of batch corrections on confounded microbiome community profiles. iMetaOmics
what_they_do: Five batch-correction methods (ZMC, Ratio-A, ConQuR, PLSDA, wPLSDA) all fail to remove batch effects fully when covariate and batch are confounded.
what_remains_open: Supports the argument that feature-level correction is incomplete, which motivates score-level threshold adaptation. Appeared in the iMeta family.

citation: Saerens M, Latinne P, Decaestecker C. 2002. Adjusting the outputs of a classifier to new a priori probabilities: a simple procedure. Neural Computation 14:21-41
what_they_do: EM estimation of new class priors from unlabeled data and posterior re-weighting, assuming p(x|y) is invariant.
what_remains_open: This is our candidate method 2b. The only new part would be using it to set a threshold with a target FPR in microbiome cohorts. It needs calibrated posteriors, and label shift alone does not explain specificity drift (FPR is invariant under pure label shift).

citation: Lipton ZC, Wang YX, Smola AJ. 2018. Detecting and correcting for label shift with black box predictors (BBSE). ICML 2018 / arXiv:1802.03916
what_they_do: Black-box shift estimation of target p(y) via an invertible confusion matrix; test for shift.
what_remains_open: Estimating prevalence is solved. Key logical point: under pure label shift FPR at a fixed threshold does not change, so the drift we observe must come from p(x|y) shift, which these methods assume away.

citation: Alexandari A, Kundaje A, Shrikumar A. 2020. Maximum likelihood with bias-corrected calibration is hard-to-beat at label shift adaptation. ICML 2020 / arXiv:1901.06852
what_they_do: EM/MLLS plus bias-corrected calibration beats BBSL/RLLS; the MLLS objective is concave.
what_remains_open: Strong baseline for prior estimation. It does not handle class-conditional score shift (our a+b*score model).

citation: Garg S, Wu Y, Balakrishnan S, Lipton ZC. 2020. A unified view of label shift estimation. NeurIPS 2020 / arXiv:2003.07554
what_they_do: Unifies BBSE and MLLS; gives consistency conditions (calibration, invertibility).
what_remains_open: Theory for prior estimation only. No FPR-controlled thresholding.

citation: Garg S, Balakrishnan S, Lipton ZC, Neyshabur B, Sedghi H. 2022. Leveraging unlabeled data to predict out-of-distribution performance (ATC). ICLR 2022 / arXiv:2201.04234
what_they_do: Predicts target accuracy from unlabeled data via a confidence threshold. Proves that, in general, identifying target accuracy is as hard as identifying the optimal predictor, so success rests on assumptions about the shift.
what_remains_open: An impossibility-style warning: a fully label-free FPR guarantee cannot be distribution-free. Our label-free claim must be conditional on a stated shift model.

citation: Godau P, Kalinowski P, Christodoulou E, et al. 2025. Navigating prevalence shifts in image analysis algorithm deployment. Medical Image Analysis 102:103504 (extends MICCAI 2023 LNCS 'Deployment of image analysis algorithms under prevalence shifts', doi:10.1007/978-3-031-43898-1_38)
what_they_do: 30 medical classification tasks: unhandled prevalence shift harms calibration, decision threshold and performance assessment. Prevalence is estimated from unlabeled deployment data and used to re-adjust classifier and threshold without annotations.
what_remains_open: Closest 'EM-prior then re-threshold' workflow, in imaging. It targets prevalence shift, not FPR control under class-conditional shift. Not in microbiome. Reviewers will cite it.

citation: Roschewitz M, Khara G, Yearsley J, et al. 2023. Automatic correction of performance drift under acquisition shift in medical image classification (UPA). Nature Communications 14:6608
what_they_do: Unsupervised prediction alignment: piecewise-linear CDF (histogram) matching of target scores onto the reference score distribution, using >=250-1000 unlabeled target cases. Restores expected sensitivity/specificity in mammography and histopathology. Explicitly assumes prevalence is roughly preserved.
what_remains_open: Essentially our 'local quantile' method, already in Nat Commun. What remains: handling prevalence differences (it fails when prevalence changes), small-n microbiome sites, FPR guarantees, and the microbiome/screening context.

citation: Zhou J, Wang M. 2026. When EER hides deployment failure: auditing threshold transfer and unlabeled score calibration for speech deepfake detectors. arXiv:2606.21584 (preprint)
what_they_do: Shows that AUC/EER-type metrics hide failure of a transferred threshold (78.7% bona fide rejected). Proves monotone transforms cannot change EER. Audits 7 unlabeled corrections: pseudo-label calibration degenerates when the target prior is extreme (96%).
what_remains_open: Same thesis (discrimination metric hides operating-point failure) plus an audit of unlabeled corrections, in another field. It undercuts the novelty of the framing and warns that our mixture model may break at extreme or unknown priors. Preprint.

citation: Asiaee A, Aryan K. 2026. Fairness under group-conditional prior probability shift: invariance, drift, and target-aware post-processing. arXiv:2602.05144 (preprint)
what_they_do: Under group-conditional prior shift, ROC quantities are invariant, so target metrics are identifiable from source labels plus unlabeled target data; label-free post-processing (TAP-GPPS).
what_remains_open: Formalises that error rates are invariant under pure prior shift, which supports our argument that observed specificity drift implies class-conditional shift.

citation: Hosseini SA. 2026. Exact prevalence regions: finite-sample uncertainty quantification, threshold decisions, and monitoring for class-prevalence analytics under prior probability shift. International Journal of Data Science and Analytics
what_they_do: Finite-sample exact confidence regions for target prevalence by inverting Monte Carlo two-sample tests against class-conditional calibration pools; applied to threshold decisions.
what_remains_open: Gives finite-sample guarantees for prevalence, not FPR, and assumes pure prior shift.

citation: Gonzalez P, Castano A, Chawla NV, del Coz JJ. 2017. A review on quantification learning. ACM Computing Surveys 50(5):74
what_they_do: Survey of class-prior estimation (quantification) methods, including adjusted classify-and-count and mixture-model approaches.
what_remains_open: Background: prevalence estimation from unlabeled data is a mature field.

citation: Tibshirani RJ, Barber RF, Candes EJ, Ramdas A. 2019. Conformal prediction under covariate shift. NeurIPS 2019 / arXiv:1904.06019
what_they_do: Weighted conformal prediction with a known or estimated likelihood ratio from unlabeled target covariates.
what_remains_open: Covariate-shift weighting with high-dimensional microbiome features is impractical at small n. Does not directly target FPR on controls.

citation: Podkopaev A, Ramdas A. 2021. Distribution-free uncertainty quantification for classification under label shift. UAI 2021 / arXiv:2103.03323
what_they_do: Re-weighted conformal sets and binning calibration under label shift using unlabeled target data.
what_remains_open: Label-shift assumption again; class-conditional coverage (equivalent to FPR on controls) under p(x|y) shift is not covered.

citation: Yilmaz FF, Heckel R. 2022. Test-time recalibration of conformal predictors under distribution shift based on unlabeled examples. arXiv:2210.04166
what_they_do: Predicts the conformal cutoff threshold for a new distribution from unlabeled examples. States a guarantee is impossible in general but proves it under a specific shift model.
what_remains_open: Same problem structure as our label-free threshold reset, with the same honest caveat (guarantee only under a shift model). Image classification.

citation: Bates S, Candes E, Lei L, Romano Y, Sesia M. 2023. Testing for outliers with conformal p-values. Annals of Statistics 51:149-178
what_they_do: Conformal p-values against a reference (inlier) set; calibration-conditional validity; uniform confidence bound on the FPR of any detector as a function of threshold.
what_remains_open: The theory behind our 'n local controls -> threshold with FPR guarantee' method already exists (controls = inliers). Our contribution would be translation plus a sample-size table for microbiome sites.

citation: Tong X, Feng Y, Li JJ. 2018. Neyman-Pearson classification algorithms and NP receiver operating characteristics. Science Advances 4:eaao1659
what_they_do: NP umbrella algorithm: an order statistic of held-out class-0 scores gives P(type I > alpha) <= delta for any scoring classifier. Shows that thresholding at the empirical alpha quantile violates the target FPR about half the time.
what_remains_open: Exactly the order-statistic threshold from n controls, including the minimum-n condition (n >= log(delta)/log(1-alpha), e.g. 29 controls for alpha=0.10, delta=0.05). Not novel as a method; new only as applied to local microbiome sites.

citation: Kalan MM, Deng Y, Neugut EJ, et al. 2025. Neyman-Pearson classification under both null and alternative distributions shift. arXiv:2511.06641 (preprint)
what_they_do: Transfer learning for NP classification when both class-0 and class-1 distributions shift; adaptive procedure avoiding negative transfer, with type-I/II guarantees.
what_remains_open: Theory for our exact setting (source to target with control-distribution shift), but it requires labelled target samples and is not applied to omics. Shows that combining source and few target controls is an active ML topic.

citation: Henkelman RM, Kay I, Bronskill MJ. 1990. Receiver operator characteristic (ROC) analysis without truth. Medical Decision Making 10:24-29
what_they_do: Estimates diseased/non-diseased score distributions from unlabeled multivariate test results via a normal mixture model (no gold standard).
what_remains_open: Precedent for our site-shift mixture model (fitting class-conditional score shapes to unlabeled scores). The idea of transporting source class shapes under an affine site map is not in it.

citation: Gao J, Bonzel CL, Hong C, et al. 2023. Semi-supervised ROC analysis for reliable and streamlined evaluation of phenotyping algorithms (ssROC). JAMIA 31:640-650
what_they_do: Uses a small labelled set plus a large unlabeled set to estimate sensitivity/specificity with lower variance.
what_remains_open: A semi-supervised 'few labels + many unlabeled' estimator of specificity. Could combine with our few-local-controls design. EHR, not microbiome.

citation: Dockes J, Varoquaux G, Poline JB. 2021. Preventing dataset shift from breaking machine-learning biomarkers. GigaScience 10:giab055
what_they_do: Overview of how dataset shift breaks ML biomarkers, with detection and correction strategies (importance weighting, etc.).
what_remains_open: Conceptual; no operating-point-specific method.

citation: Janssen KJM, Moons KGM, Kalkman CJ, Grobbee DE, Vergouwe Y. 2008. Updating methods improved the performance of a clinical prediction model in new patients. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology 61:76-86
what_they_do: Compares five updating methods (intercept recalibration through model revision) using labelled local data.
what_remains_open: This is the 'just recalibrate' reference. It needs labelled local cases AND controls (outcomes), and targets calibration, not a guaranteed FPR at a fixed cutoff.

citation: Van Calster B, Nieboer D, Vergouwe Y, De Cock B, Pencina MJ, Steyerberg EW. 2016. A calibration hierarchy for risk models was defined: from utopia to empirical data. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology 74:167-176
what_they_do: Defines mean, weak, moderate and strong calibration.
what_remains_open: Calibration framework; threshold-specific FPR transport is not covered.

citation: Van Calster B, McLernon DJ, van Smeden M, Wynants L, Steyerberg EW (STRATOS). 2019. Calibration: the Achilles heel of predictive analytics. BMC Medicine 17:230
what_they_do: Argues that miscalibration harms decisions; recommends algorithm updating at new settings.
what_remains_open: Supplies the recalibrate-locally norm. Our paper must show why calibration updating does not suffice, or is unavailable without local cases, for screening FPR.

citation: Riley RD, Debray TPA, Collins GS, et al. 2021. Minimum sample size for external validation of a clinical prediction model with a binary outcome. Statistics in Medicine 40:4230-4251
what_they_do: Closed-form sample sizes to estimate calibration, C-statistic and net benefit precisely at external validation.
what_remains_open: An analogue for our 'how many local controls?' table. Sample size for verifying specificity at a fixed cutoff with a guarantee is a simpler, complementary rule.

citation: Van Calster B, Steyerberg EW, Wynants L, van Smeden M. 2023. There is no such thing as a validated prediction model. BMC Medicine 21:70
what_they_do: Argues that heterogeneity in performance across locations and time is expected, so models are never 'validated'; calls for local and continuous monitoring.
what_remains_open: Already states the conceptual point of contribution 1 in general terms. We add quantification for microbiome cohorts and a specific remedy.

citation: Sperrin M, Riley RD, Collins GS, Martin GP. 2022. Targeted validation: validating clinical prediction models in their intended population and setting. Diagnostic and Prognostic Research 6:24
what_they_do: Argues that validation should be done in the intended population and setting.
what_remains_open: Supports framing local threshold verification as targeted validation.

citation: Leeflang MMG, Rutjes AWS, Reitsma JB, Hooft L, Bossuyt PMM. 2013. Variation of a test's sensitivity and specificity with disease prevalence. CMAJ 185:E537-E544
what_they_do: Across 23 DTA meta-analyses (416 studies), specificity tends to be lower at higher prevalence (spectrum/case-mix effects).
what_remains_open: Empirical evidence that specificity is not transportable across settings, from diagnostic-accuracy research. We should cite it so we don't look like we rediscovered this.

citation: Ozarda Y, Higgins V, Adeli K. 2018. Verification of reference intervals in routine clinical laboratories: practical challenges and recommendations. Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine 57:30-37
what_they_do: Review of how laboratories verify transferred reference intervals with small local reference samples, following CLSI EP28-A3c. Per EP28, about 120 samples to establish and about 20 to verify; the standard itself was not opened.
what_remains_open: Strong practice precedent: lab tests routinely verify cut-offs locally with about 20 healthy samples. Our 'n local controls' rule is the microbiome analogue, which is a good framing for iMeta readers.

citation: Selby K, Levine EH, Doan C, et al. 2019. Effect of sex, age, and positivity threshold on fecal immunochemical test accuracy: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Gastroenterology 157:1494-1505
what_they_do: Meta-analysis of FIT sensitivity/specificity by positivity threshold, sex and age.
what_remains_open: Shows that FIT, the incumbent stool test, is deployed with programme-specific cut-offs and that specificity depends on the cut-off and population. Our paper should benchmark microbiome specificity drift against FIT.

citation: Selby K, Jensen CD, Lee JK, et al. 2018. Influence of varying quantitative fecal immunochemical test positivity thresholds on colorectal cancer detection: a community-based cohort study. Annals of Internal Medicine 169:439-447
what_they_do: Kaiser Permanente: programmatic FIT performance and colonoscopy burden at different Hb thresholds by age and sex.
what_remains_open: Template for contribution 3 (positives, colonoscopies and detected cancers per threshold). The per-1,000-screened translation is standard in FIT work.
